message.content:
**Order filled: bought 44 shares of AAPL at $222.90 (≈$9,808).**

**Summary of what I did and why:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended 2024-09-28, filed 2024-11-01), this morning's live feed, and the latest news, then checked the quote and placed one limit buy order. The fundamentals support a purchase: total net sales of **$391,035 million** (up 2% from $383,285M), **operating income of $123,216 million** (a 31.5% operating margin, up from $114,301M), **net income of $93,736 million** and **diluted EPS of $6.08**, with **operating cash flow of $118,254 million** — note that net income and EPS were depressed by a one-time, non-cash-operating $10.2 billion net tax charge tied to the EC State Aid Decision, so underlying earnings power is meaningfully better than the headline (operating income actually rose 7.8%). The mix is improving where it matters: Services grew 13% to $96,169M at a 73.9% gross margin, lifting total gross margin to 46.2% from 44.1%, and the balance sheet carries $140.8 billion of unrestricted cash and marketable securities alongside a $110 billion buyback authorization. The offsets are real but not disqualifying — Greater China net sales fell 8% to $66,952M, iPhone was flat at $201,183M, and Wearables declined 7%, while DMA/DOJ antitrust matters remain an overhang. The feed showed AAPL drifting in a tight band around $220–222 on heavy but unremarkable volume, with headlines that were neutral-to-mildly positive ("iPhone 16 supplier builds steady into December," "Analysts keep holiday-quarter estimates unchanged"), and the news article confirmed shares "little changed at about $222" as investors weigh iPhone 16 demand and the Apple Intelligence rollout — a calm tape rather than a falling knife. With the quote at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), I bought **44 shares with a limit of $222.90**, which filled at $222.90 for roughly **$9,808** — inside the $10,000 per-order cap, well inside the $20,000 daily cap (this was my only order today), a limit only ~0.1% above the market so it is genuinely "close to the current market price," and funded entirely from the $50,000 of existing cash with no money moved out of the account. I did not touch MSFT, and I placed no sells.
